caption: The drawing depicts a lidded urn or trophy-like vessel, rendered in shades of gray, depicting it as a silvery metallic object with reflective surfaces and intricate engraved or embossed patterns. The urn has a rounded base that sits atop a square plinth, a bulbous, tapering body with vertical fluting, a flared rim, and a domed lid topped with a finial shaped like a pinecone or acorn. Surrounding the base of the vessel, there is an ornamental border with repeated patterns, and on the body of the urn, stylized decorative motifs are visible, including garland and medallion designs. Below the main image, smaller technical drawings are included, such as a detailed section of the ornamental border, a triangular composition of the upper design, an oval maker's mark, a narrow rectangular stamp, and additional schematics of the vessel's design elements and proportions. The background is a plain, light beige color, and the artist's name, "Harold E. Walsh," is written to the lower right of the main urn drawing.
title: Silver Sugar Urn
